en: Something that restrains, ties, fastens or secures.
Control or caution; reserve.

restraint.ety: From Middle English restreynte, from Old French restreinte; more at restrain.

ex.en: She was angry, but she spoke with restraint.
ex.ja: 彼女は怒っていたが、それをおさえて話をした。

ex.en: He refused to exercise self-restraint.
ex.ja: 彼は自粛の波に乗らなかった。

ex.en: Institutionally, a major restraint is the copyright problem.
ex.ja: 制度的に大きな枷となるのは、著作権の問題である。

note.ja: restrain（抑える）+ -t。re + stringere（締める）。「抑制・自制・拘束」。strict と同系。

en: A chasm or fissure.
A lack of cohesion; a state of conflict, incompatibility, or emotional distance.
To form a rift; to split open.
To cleave; to rive; to split.

rift.ety: From Middle English rift, of North Germanic origin; akin to Danish rift, Norwegian Bokmål rift (“breach”), Old Norse rífa (“to tear”). More at rive.

ex.en: The argument caused a rift between the two friends.
ex.ja: その口論で二人の友人の仲に亀裂が入った。

note.ja: 北欧語 ript（裂け目）から。rive（裂く）と同系。「亀裂・不和」。

en: A man whose job it is to sell things, either in a shop / store or elsewhere.

salesman.ety:
Etymology tree
English sales
Proto-Indo-European *mon-
Proto-Germanic *mann-
Proto-West Germanic *mann
Old English mann
Middle English man
Middle English -man
English -man
English salesman
From sales + -man.

ex.en: The old man was taken in by a salesman.
ex.ja: その老人はセールスマンにだまされた。

ex.en: I was taken in by the salesman.
ex.ja: 私はそのセールスマンにだまされたんだ。

ex.en: He makes a living as a salesman.
ex.ja: 彼はセールスマンをして生計をたてている。

note.ja: sale（販売）+ s + man。「販売員」。

en: A brilliant red colour sometimes tinged with orange.
Cloth of a scarlet color.
Of a bright red colour.
Sinful or whorish.
To dye or tinge (something) with scarlet.

scarlet.ety: From Middle English scarlet, scarlat, borrowed from Old French escarlate (“a type of cloth”), from Medieval Latin scarlātum (“scarlet cloth”), of uncertain origin. This was long thought to derive from Classical Persian سقرلات (saqirlāt, “a warm woollen cloth”), but the Persian word (first attested in the 1290s) is now thought to be from Arabic سِقِلَّات (siqillāt), denoting very expensive, luxury silks dyed scarlet-red using the exceptionally expensive dye, first attested around the ninth century. The most obvious route for the Arabic word siqillāt to have entered the Romance languages would b

ex.en: She wore a scarlet dress to the party.
ex.ja: 彼女は緋色のドレスを着てパーティーに行った。

note.ja: 中世ラテン語 scarlata（高価な布）から。ペルシャ語とされる。「緋色」。

en: A pipe or channel, or system of pipes or channels, used to remove human waste and to provide drainage.
To provide (a place) with a system of sewers.

sewer.ety: From Middle English sewer, seuer, from Anglo-Norman sewere (“water-course”), from Old French sewiere (“overflow channel for a fishpond”), from Vulgar Latin *exaquāria (“drain for carrying water off”), from Latin ex (“out of, from”) + aquāria (“of or pertaining to waters”) or from a root *exaquāre.

ex.en: The city is repairing its old sewers.
ex.ja: 市は古い下水道を修理している。

note.ja: 古フランス語 esseweur（排水路）から。ex + aqua（水）。「水を外へ出す所」→「下水道」。縫う人の sewer（ソウアー）は別語。

en: A distinct flavor, especially if slight.
A slight trace of something; a smattering.
To get the flavor of.
To have a particular taste; used with of.
As if with a smack or slap; smartly; sharply.

smack.ety:
The noun is from Middle English smac, smak, smacke, from Old English smæc, smæċċ (“taste, smatch”), from Proto-West Germanic *smakku, from Proto-Germanic *smakkuz (“a taste”), from Proto-Indo-European *smegʰ-, *smeg- (“to taste”). The verb is from Middle English smaken. Doublet of smatch (obsolete, “taste”; q.v.), from Old English smæċċan (“to taste, smack”).
Cognate with Scots smak (“scent, smell, taste, flavour”), Saterland Frisian Smoak (“taste”), West Frisian smaak (“taste”), Dutch smaak (“taste”), German Schmack, Geschmack (“taste”), Danish smag (“taste”), Swedish and Norwegian smak (“tas

ex.en: She smacked him across the face.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼の顔に平手打ちを食わせた。

ex.en: I'll smack the living daylights out of you!
ex.ja: ぶっ飛ばしてやる！

ex.en: This soup smacks of fish.
ex.ja: このスープは魚の味がする。

note.ja: 「ぴしゃりと打つ」は擬音語。「味がする（smack of）」は古英語 smæc（味）からで別語。

en: Of or pertaining to the southwest.

southwestern.ety: From Middle English southwesterne, from Old English sūþwesterne, equivalent to south + western.

ex.en: They live in a small town in southwestern France.
ex.ja: 彼らはフランス南西部の小さな町に住んでいる。

note.ja: south + west + -ern。「南西の」。

en: A person who acts as the voice of another person or a group of people.

spokesperson.ety: From spoke (“past participle of speak”) + -s- + person.

ex.en: A spokesperson for the company answered questions.
ex.ja: その会社の広報担当者が質問に答えた。

note.ja: spokesman を性別に中立にした語。「報道官」。

en: The act of going stealthily.
Hunting for game by moving silently and stealthily or by waiting in ambush.

stalking.ety: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

ex.en: Stalking is a serious crime.
ex.ja: ストーカー行為は重大な犯罪だ。

note.ja: stalk（忍び寄る）+ -ing。stalk は steal（盗む・こっそり動く）と同系。「ストーカー行為」。

en: Designed or constructed in a standard manner or according to an official standard.

ex.en: All students took a standardized test.
ex.ja: 全生徒が統一テストを受けた。

note.ja: standardize（標準化する）+ -ed。standard と同じ。

en: A single pass of a needle in sewing; the loop or turn of the thread thus made.
A single pass of a surgical suture (to sew the edges of a wound together)
To form stitches in; especially, to sew in such a manner as to show on the surface a continuous line of stitches.
To sew, or unite or attach by stitches.

stitch.ety:
From Middle English stiche, from Old English stiċe (“a prick, puncture, stab, thrust with a pointed implement, pricking sensation, stitch, pain in the side, sting”), from Proto-West Germanic *stiki, from Proto-Germanic *stikiz (“prick, piercing, stitch”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)teyg- (“to stab, pierce”).
Cognate with Dutch steek (“prick, stitch”), German Stich (“a prick, piercing, stitch”), Old English stician (“to stick, stab, pierce, prick”). More at stick. Via PIE cognate with Czech steh, Polish ścieg, Russian стежо́к (stežók).

ex.en: He didn't do a stitch of work.
ex.ja: 彼は少しも仕事をしなかった。

ex.en: Your stitches will be removed in a few days.
ex.ja: 抜糸は数日後になります。

ex.en: You're going to need a few stitches.
ex.ja: 何針か、縫わないといけないですね。

note.ja: 古英語 stice（刺すこと）から。stick（刺す）と同系。「縫い目・ひと針」。A stitch in time saves nine.（早めの一針は九針の手間を省く）。

en: An underlying layer; a substratum.
The substance lining the bottom edge of an enclosure.
Having very slight furrows.

ex.en: Mushrooms grow on a substrate of wood chips.
ex.ja: キノコは木くずの培地の上で育つ。

note.ja: ラテン語 substratum（下に敷かれたもの）から。sub + sternere（広げる）。「下層・基板・基質」。

ja: スルタン（イスラム国家の君主）

en: The holder of a secular office, formally subordinate to, but de facto the power behind the throne of, the caliph.
A hereditary ruler in various Muslim states (sultanate), varying from petty principalities (as in Yemen), often vassal of a greater ruler…

sultan.ety:
Etymology tree

Borrowed from Middle French sultan or Medieval Latin sultanus, from Ottoman Turkish سلطان (sultan), from Arabic سُلْطَان (sulṭān, “strength, authority, ruler”). Compare Hebrew שִׁלְטוֹן (shiltón) and סוּלְטָן (sultán). Doublet of soldan.

ex.en: Once the Sultan ruled over what today is Turkey.
ex.ja: かつてサルタンが今日のトルコを統治していた。

note.ja: アラビア語 sulṭān（権力・支配者）から。「スルタン」。

en: The quality of being supreme.
Power over all others.

supremacy.ety: From supreme + -acy (a variant of -cy). Compare with supremity and New Latin suprematia.

ex.en: The two companies fought for supremacy in the market.
ex.ja: 二つの会社は市場の覇権を争った。

note.ja: ラテン語 supremus（最も上の）から。→「優位・覇権・至上」。supreme（最高の）。

en: To become larger, fuller, or rounder, or expand in size or shape, usually as a result of pressure from within.
To cause to become bigger.
The act of swelling; increase in size.
A bulge or protuberance.
Very well.

swell.ety:
From Middle English swellen, from Old English swellan (“to swell”), from Proto-West Germanic *swellan, from Proto-Germanic *swellaną (“to swell”), of unknown origin.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian swälle (“to swell”), West Frisian swolle (“to swell”), Dutch zwellen (“to swell”), Low German swellen (“to swell”), German schwellen (“to swell”), Swedish svälla (“to swell”), Icelandic svella. The adjective may derive from the noun.

ex.en: My hands and legs are swollen.
ex.ja: 手足がむくんでいます。

ex.en: My hands became swollen up while taking a long bath.
ex.ja: 長くお風呂に入っていたら手がふやけてしまった。

ex.en: My tongue is swollen, and I can't taste a thing!
ex.ja: 舌が腫れて、味覚がない！

note.ja: 古英語 swellan（膨らむ）から。「膨らむ・腫れる」→ 大波 →（俗）「すてきな」。

en: In theory; on paper.
In a theoretical manner.

theoretically.ety:

English theoretical

English theoretically
From theoretical + -ly.

ex.en: Theoretically, I'm doing math.
ex.ja: 理論的には、私は数学をしている。

note.ja: theoretical（理論的な）+ -ly。theory はギリシャ語 theōria（眺めること）。

en: A sensation of dryness in the throat associated with a craving for liquids, produced by deprivation of drink, or by some other cause (suc…
The condition producing the sensation of thirst.
To be thirsty.
To desire vehemently.

thirst.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-West Germanic *þurstu
Old English þurst
Old English þyrstaninflu.
Middle English thirst
English thirst
From Middle English thirst, thurst, from Old English þurst, from Proto-West Germanic *þurstu, from Proto-Germanic *þurstuz, from Proto-Indo-European *ters- (“dry”).
Germanic cognates include Old High German thurst, Middle High German durst, German Durst, Old Saxon thurst, Old Dutch thursti, Middle Dutch dorst, dorste, Dutch dorst, Old Norse þorsti (Swedish törst, Icelandic þorsti, Faroese tosti, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål tørst, Norwegian Nynorsk tørste). Indo-European c

ex.en: The man died of thirst in a dry country.
ex.ja: その男はある乾燥した国で水が飲めずに死んだ。

ex.en: I'm dying of thirst. Give me water!
ex.ja: 喉が渇いて死にそうだよ。水をくれ！

ex.en: I'm dying of thirst at the moment.
ex.ja: 差し当たり喉が渇いて死にそうだよ。

note.ja: 古英語 thurst から。ドイツ語 Durst と同じ。「のどの渇き」→「渇望」。

en: of, or relating to a transition
temporary; pending the implementation of something new

transitional.ety:

From transition + -al.

ex.en: The need for a transitional object is not an illness.
ex.ja: ブランケット症候群は、病気ではありません。

note.ja: transition（移行）+ -al。「過渡的な」。

en: Any of several species of fish of the genus Thunnus in the family Scombridae.
The edible flesh of the tuna.

tuna.ety:
Etymology tree
Phoenicianbor.
Ancient Greek θῠ́ννος (thŭ́nnos)bor.
Latin thunnusbor.
Arabic تُنّ (tunn)
Andalusian Arabicbor.
Old Spanish atun
Spanish atúnder.
United States Spanish tunabor.
English tuna
Borrowed from United States Spanish tuna, alteration of Spanish atún, from Arabic التُّنّ (at-tunn, “tuna”), from Latin thunnus, itself from Ancient Greek θύννος (thúnnos). Possibly in the sense of "darter" from thynein "to dart along". Doublet of tonno.

ex.en: The tuna catch is declining.
ex.ja: マグロの漁獲量は減ってきている。

ex.en: Tom ate a tuna sandwich.
ex.ja: トムはツナサンドを食べたんだ。

ex.en: I've been having tuna and mayo onigiri recently.
ex.ja: 最近はツナマヨおにぎり。

note.ja: スペイン語 atún（アラビア語 at-tūn）から。ラテン語 thunnus。

en: Not used.
Not accustomed (to), unfamiliar with.

unused.ety:
Etymology tree

Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Proto-Germanic *un-
Proto-West Germanic *un-
Old English un-
Middle English un-
English un-
English used
English unused
From un- + used.

ex.en: We have two unused rooms in our house.
ex.ja: 私たちの家には、使われていない部屋が二つあります。

ex.en: We have vast amounts of unused information.
ex.ja: 私たちには、まだ使っていない極めて多量の情報がある。

note.ja: un（否定）+ used（使われた）。「使われていない」。

en: The position from which something is observed or considered
An angle, outlook or point of view.

ex.en: An extensive viewpoint that covers everything is important.
ex.ja: 全体を見渡す視点が大事。

ex.en: Traditional viewpoints gave way to new ones.
ex.ja: 伝統的な見方が新しい見方に取って代わられた。

ex.en: I am looking at the matter from a different viewpoint.
ex.ja: 私は違った観点からその問題を見ています。

note.ja: view（見ること）+ point（地点）。「見る地点」→「観点」。

en: A sour liquid formed by the fermentation of alcohol used as a condiment or preservative; a dilute solution of acetic acid.
Any variety of vinegar.
To season or otherwise treat with vinegar.

vinegar.ety:
Etymology tree

Late Latin ācrus
Old French aigre
Old French vinaigrebor.
Middle English vynegre
English vinegar
From Middle English vynegre, from Old French vinaigre from Old French vyn egre, based on Latin vīnum (“wine”) + Latin ācer (“sour”). Displaced Old English æċed (survived in Middle English eced).

ex.en: Please bring me vinegar and oil.
ex.ja: お酢と油を持ってきてください。

ex.en: Did you know that vinegar can be made from dates?
ex.ja: デーツからお酢ができるって、知ってた？

ex.en: Vinegar has a sharp taste.
ex.ja: 酢はすっぱい味がする。

note.ja: 古フランス語 vin aigre（酸っぱいワイン）から。vin（ワイン）+ aigre（酸っぱい）。wine、eager と同じ。

en: A head of real or synthetic hair worn on the head to disguise baldness, for cultural or religious reasons, for fashion, or by actors to h…
A bigwig.
To put on a wig; to provide with a wig (especially of an actor etc.).
To upbraid, reprimand.

wig.ety: Clipping of periwig, itself an alteration of French perruque. The meaning of "to reprimand" perhaps came from this being something a bigwig would do or perhaps from the expressions to flip one's wig, wigs on the green, or dash my wig!

ex.en: Tom used to wear a wig.
ex.ja: トムは昔、かつらをつけていた。

ex.en: Don't tell anybody else, but director Tanaka wears a wig.
ex.ja: ここだけの話だけど、田中部長、実はカツラなんだって。

note.ja: periwig（かつら）の短縮。フランス語 perruque。

en: The relationship resulting from affiliating one thing with another.
The establishment of a child's paternity or maternity.

affiliation.ety: From French affiliation, from Latin affiliatiō, noun of action from verb affiliō, from af- (form of ad- (“to”) before an f) + filiō (from filius (“son”)).

ex.en: He has no political affiliation.
ex.ja: 彼はどの政党にも所属していない。

note.ja: affiliate（提携させる）+ -ion。ad + filius（息子）。「養子にすること」→「所属・提携」。

en: In an aggressive manner.

aggressively.ety:

From aggressive + -ly.

ex.en: I am really aggressively looking for a boyfriend.
ex.ja: 私ガンガン男狙ってまっせ〜

note.ja: ag（〜へ）+ gress（歩む）+ ive + ly。攻め寄るように →「攻撃的に・積極的に」。

en: To form a line; to fall into line.
To adjust to a line; to range or form in line; to bring into line.

align.ety: From Middle English alynen, alinen (“copulate”), from Middle French aligner, from Old French alignier, from a- + lignier, from Latin lineare (“make straight or perpendicular”), from the noun linea (“line”), from līneus (“flaxen; flaxen [thing]”), from līnum (“flax”), likely ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *līnom (compare linen).

ex.en: Align the text to the left side of the page.
ex.ja: 文字をページの左側にそろえてください。

note.ja: フランス語 aligner ＝ à（〜に）+ ligne（線）。「線にそろえる」→「一致させる・提携する」。

en: A disorder of the immune system causing adverse reactions to substances (allergens) not harmful to most and marked by the body's producti…
Specifically, hypersensitivity of class I in the modern classification thereof: the immunoglobulin E–mediated type.

allergy.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₂el-der.
Proto-Indo-European *h₂élyos
Proto-Hellenic *ál͏̌l͏̌os
Ancient Greek ᾰ̓́λλος (ắllos)

Proto-Hellenic *wérgon

English allergy
Borrowed from German Allergie. Coined by Austrian pediatrician Clemens von Pirquet in 1906 from Ancient Greek ἄλλος (állos, “other”) + ἔργον (érgon, “work, activity”), on the model of Energie.

ex.en: A lot of people are dealing with allergies now.
ex.ja: 近頃は多くの人がアレルギーを持っている。

ex.en: I have an allergy to milk.
ex.ja: ミルクアレルギーなんです。

ex.en: Do you have any food allergies?
ex.ja: 何か食べ物にアレルギーはありますか？

note.ja: ドイツ語 Allergie から。ギリシャ語 allos（ほかの）+ ergon（働き）。「異なる反応」→「アレルギー」。energy と同じ erg。

en: Forgetfulness; cessation of remembrance of wrong; oblivion.
An act of the sovereign power granting oblivion, or a general pardon, for a past offense, as to subjects concerned in an insurrection.
To grant a pardon (to a group).

amnesty.ety: Borrowed from Middle French amnestie (Modern French amnistie), a borrowing from Latin amnestia, itself a borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀμνηστία (amnēstía).

ex.en: They should be pardoned by the amnesty law.
ex.ja: 彼らは恩赦法によって許されるはずだ。

ex.en: Amnesty International often organizes public protests in support of political prisoners.
ex.ja: 国際アムネスティは、政治囚への支援として一般市民による抗議活動を組織することがしばしばある。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 amnēstia（忘れること）から。a（否定）+ mnasthai（覚えている）。「（罪を）忘れること」→「恩赦」。amnesia（記憶喪失）も同じ。

en: The act of asserting; positive declaration or averment.
Something which is asserted; a declaration; a statement asserted.

assertion.ety: From Middle English assercioun, from Latin assertiō. By surface analysis, assert + -ion.

ex.en: Nobody will believe his assertion that he is innocent.
ex.ja: 無実だという彼の主張は誰も信じないだろう。

ex.en: It is important to note that his assertion is groundless.
ex.ja: 彼の主張には根拠がないことに注意することが重要である。

note.ja: assert（主張する）+ -ion。ラテン語 asserere ＝ ad + serere（つなぐ）。「自分に結びつける」→「主張」。

en: The study of the physical universe beyond the Earth's atmosphere, including the process of mapping locations and properties of the matter…

astronomy.ety: From Middle English astronomie, astronemy, from Old French astronomie, equivalent to astro- + -nomy. Displaced native Old English tungolcræft.

ex.en: Astronomy is by no means a new science.
ex.ja: 天文学は決して新しい科学ではない。

ex.en: He studies astronomy, or the science of stars.
ex.ja: 彼は天文学、すなわち星の研究をしている。

ex.en: It seems that he is interested in astronomy.
ex.ja: 彼は天文学に興味があるようだ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 astron（星）+ nomos（法則）。「星の法則」→「天文学」。astrology（星の学 → 占星術）と区別。

en: On the top of.

atop.ety:

From a- (“on”) + top.

ex.en: There's a bird atop that tree.
ex.ja: あそこの木の上に鳥がいます。

Guma derives from Proto-Germanic *gumô (“man, person”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰǵʰm̥mō; it is cognate to Icelandic gumi (cf. Icelandic brúðgumi) and Norwegian gume and, ultimately, human.

By the 1930s, the present use of the plurale tantum "lyrics" had begun; it has been standard sin

squash.ety: From Middle English squachen, squatchen, from Old French esquacher, escachier, from Vulgar Latin *excoāctiāre, from Latin ex + coāctāre. Probably influenced by Middle English quashen, quassen, from Old French esquasser, escasser (“to crush, shatter, destroy, break”), from Vulgar Latin *exquassare, from Latin ex- + quassare (“to shatter”) (see quash).

ex.en: I'd like to play a game of squash.
ex.ja: スカッシュをしたいのですが。

ex.en: I took up squash only a few months ago.
ex.ja: 数ヶ月前にスカッシュを始めたばかりなんだ。

ex.en: The University grounds include a squash court.
ex.ja: 大学は敷地内にスカッシュコートを完備しています。

note.ja: 「押しつぶす」は古フランス語 esquasser から。カボチャの squash はアメリカ先住民の言葉からで別語。

en: Happening in or affecting an entire state (political subdivision of a federal union).
Happening in or affecting an entire sovereign state; nationwide.
Throughout a state (political subdivision of a federal union).
Throughout a sovereign state; nationwide.
An agency or association operating through a state (political subdivision).

ex.ja: 知事は州全体で木を植える計画を発表した。

en: Not moving.
Incapable of being moved.

stationary.ety: From Latin stationarius, from statio, ultimately from stō (“to stand”). Doublet of stationer. Equivalent to station + -ary.

ex.en: The population remains stationary.
ex.ja: 人口は変動しないでいる。

note.ja: ラテン語 stationarius（立ち止まった）から。stare（立つ）。「静止した」。stationery（文房具）と綴りが1字違い。

en: A division into smaller pieces of something that has already been divided.
Such a piece that has been divided.
To separate something into smaller pieces.

From sub- + division.

ex.ja: 彼らは郊外の新しい分譲地に住んでいる。

note.ja: sub（下に）+ division（区分）。「さらに細かく分けること」→「細分化・分譲地」。

en: Coal tar.
(often typeset "tar" in USA) A solid residual byproduct of tobacco smoke.
To coat with tar.
To besmirch.

From Middle English ter, terr, tarr, from Old English teoru, from Proto-West Germanic *teru, from Proto-Germanic *terwą, from Proto-Indo-European *derwo-, from *dóru (“tree”).
See also Saterland Frisian Taar, West Frisian tarre, tar, Dutch teer, German Teer; also Welsh derw (“oaks”), Lithuanian dervà (“pinewood, resin”), Russian де́рево (dérevo, “tree”), Bulgarian дърво́ (dărvó, “tree”). More at tree.

ex.en: The components obtained by distillation of coal tar are as shown below.
ex.ja: コールタールを蒸留して得られる成分名は下表の通りである。

note.ja: 古英語 teoru（樹脂）から。tree と同系。「タール」。

en: A system of government-imposed duties levied on imported or exported goods; a list of such duties, or the duties themselves.
A schedule of rates, fees or prices.
To levy a duty on (something).

tariff.ety: From Italian tariffa (“arithmetical table; list of customs duties”), from Arabic تَعْرِيف (taʕrīf, “notification, explanation”). Equivalent to Portuguese and Spanish tarifa and the French tarif and first attested in 1592.

ex.en: We hope to lower the tariff.
ex.ja: 関税を下げることを望む。

ex.en: High tariffs have become a barrier to international trade.
ex.ja: 高い関税が国際貿易の障害となっている。

ex.en: High tariffs are the chief obstacles to free trade.
ex.ja: 高関税が自由貿易への最大の障害になっている。

note.ja: アラビア語 taʿrīf（通知・料金表）から、イタリア語を経た語。「関税」。

en: Of or relating to the material world, as opposed to sacred or clerical.
Of limited time, transient, passing, not perpetual, as opposed to eternal.
Anything temporal or secular; a temporality.

temporal.ety: From Middle English temporal, temporel (“transitory, worldly, material, of secular society”), from Old French temporel or Latin temporālis (“of time (in grammar), temporary, relating to time as opposed to eternity”), from tempus (“time, period, opportunity”) + -ālis.

ex.en: The study looks at temporal changes in the climate.
ex.ja: その研究は気候の時間的な変化を調べている。

note.ja: ラテン語 temporalis（時の）から。tempus（時）。「時間の・現世の」。「こめかみの」はラテン語 tempora（こめかみ）からで別語。

en: Any of various rotary machines that use the kinetic energy of a continuous stream of fluid (a liquid or a gas) to turn a shaft.

turbine.ety: Borrowed from French turbine, from Latin turbō, turbinem (“tornado, whirlwind; crowd”).

ex.en: The wind turbine turns slowly in the breeze.
ex.ja: 風力タービンがそよ風の中でゆっくり回っている。

note.ja: ラテン語 turbo（渦・こま）から。turb（かき乱す・回る）。→「タービン」。

en: Not available.
A communist who operated underground and was therefore not available for a political leadership position.

Proto-West Germanic *un-
Old English un-

English unavailable
From un- + available.

ex.en: The manager is unavailable at the moment.
ex.ja: 支配人は今、手が離せません。

note.ja: un（否定）+ available（利用できる）。「利用できない・手が空いていない」。

en: In a universal manner.
By everyone or by the vast majority of people.

universally.ety: From Middle English universally; equivalent to universal + -ly.

ex.en: Minecraft has been a universally loved game for years.
ex.ja: マインクラフトは長年世界中から愛される定番ゲームです。

note.ja: universal + -ly。「普遍的に」。

en: Unfortunate, marked by misfortune.
Inauspicious.

unlucky.ety:
Etymology tree

From un- + lucky.

ex.en: Four is an unlucky number in Japan.
ex.ja: ４は日本では不吉な数字だ。

ex.en: Today is an unlucky day, isn't it?
ex.ja: はあ、今日はついてないなあ。

note.ja: un（否定）+ lucky（幸運な）。「運の悪い」。

en: The act of one who vomits.
The matter that is vomited.

ex.en: How often have you been vomiting?
ex.ja: どれくらいの頻度で嘔吐してますか？

ex.en: I feel like vomiting.
ex.ja: 胸がムカムカします。

ex.en: Large residual stomach contents may lead to loss of appetite, nausea and vomiting.
ex.ja: 胃の内容物の残存量が多いと、 食欲不振 、 吐 き気および嘔吐が強くなる。

note.ja: vomit（吐く）+ -ing。ラテン語 vomere（吐く）。「嘔吐」。

en: A chief administrative officer of a prison.
An official charged with supervisory duties or with the enforcement of specific laws or regulations; such as a game warden or air-raid wa…
To carry out the duties of a warden.

warden.ety: From Middle English wardein, from Anglo-Norman wardein, from warder (“to guard”), variant of Old French guarder (“to guard”) (whence modern French garder, also English guard), from Proto-Germanic *wardāną; related to Old High German wartēn (“to watch”). Compare guardian, French gardien, from Old French guardian, guardein. Compare also ward and reward. Doublet of guardian.

ex.en: There was only one warden on duty when the riot started.
ex.ja: 暴動が起こったとき、当直の監視員はたった１人だった。

note.ja: 古北フランス語 wardein（守る人）から。guardian と同じ語源。「管理人・刑務所長」。

en: The state, quality, or condition of being physically bent or twisted out of shape.
The state, quality, or condition of being deviant from what is right or proper morally or mentally.
To twist or turn (something) out of shape; to deform.
To become twisted out of shape; to deform.

warp.ety:
From Middle English warp, werp, from Old English wearp, warp (“a warp, threads stretched lengthwise in a loom, twig, osier”), from Proto-Germanic *warpą (“a warp”).
Cognate with Middle Dutch warp, Middle Low German warp, German werfen, Danish and Swedish varp.

ex.en: The heat warped the plastic case.
ex.ja: 熱でプラスチックのケースがゆがんだ。

note.ja: 古英語 weorpan（投げる・曲げる）から。「ゆがめる」、織機に張る「縦糸」。SF の warp（空間をゆがめる）も同じ。

en: In female mammals, the organ in which the young are conceived and grow until birth; the uterus.
A place where something is made or formed.

womb.ety: From Middle English wombe, wambe, from Old English womb, wamb (“belly, stomach; bowels; heart; womb; hollow”), from Proto-West Germanic *wambu, from Proto-Germanic *wambō (“belly, stomach, abdomen”). Cognate with Scots wam, wame (“womb”), Dutch wam (“dewlap of beef; belly of a fish”), German Wamme, Wampe (“paunch, belly”), Danish vom (“belly, paunch, rumen”), Swedish våmb (“belly, stomach, rumen”), Norwegian vom (“rumen”), Icelandic vömb (“belly, abdomen, stomach”), Old Welsh gumbelauc (“womb”), Breton gwamm (“woman, wife”), Sanskrit वपा (vapā́, “the skin or membrane lining the intestines or p

ex.en: The child followeth the womb.
ex.ja: 子供は子宮に従う。

ex.en: The national health service takes care of you from womb to tomb.
ex.ja: 国民保健サービスは、生涯に渡ってあなたのお世話を致します。

ex.en: Babies grow up inside the amniotic fluid in the womb.
ex.ja: 赤ちゃんは子宮内の羊水で発育します。

note.ja: 古英語 wamb（腹）から。「子宮」。

en: A milk-based product stiffened by a bacterium-aided curdling process, and sometimes mixed with fruit or other flavoring.
Any similar product based on other substances (e.g. soy yogurt).

yogurt.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Turkic *yogrut
Ottoman Turkish یوغورت (yoğurt)bor.
English yogurt
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish یوغورت (yoğurt). Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *yogrut.

ex.en: This yogurt is sweet.
ex.ja: このヨーグルト、甘いね。

ex.en: I'm buying different yogurt every month to see what I like most.
ex.ja: 自分にあったヨーグルトを選ぶため、毎月違うものを買っている。

ex.en: Do you like yogurt?
ex.ja: ヨーグルトはお好きですか？

note.ja: トルコ語 yoğurt から。yoğurmak（こねる・濃くする）。

en: To end a law, system, institution, custom or practice.

abolish.ety: From late Middle English abolisshen, from Middle French aboliss-, extended stem of abolir, from Latin abolēre (“to retard, check the growth of, (and by extension) destroy, abolish”), and inchoative abolēscere (“to wither, vanish, cease”).

ex.en: I thought that system was abolished last year.
ex.ja: そのシステムは去年廃止されたはずです。

ex.en: I thought that that system was abolished last year.
ex.ja: そのシステムは去年廃止されたはずです。

ex.en: This evil custom must be abolished.
ex.ja: この悪い習慣は廃止しなければならない。

note.ja: ラテン語 abolere（滅ぼす）から。「廃止する」。abolition（奴隷制の廃止）。

en: Of, relating to, or inhabiting mountains, especially above the timberline.
Of or relating to slalom and downhill skiing.
Any of several plants, native to mountain habitats, often grown in rock gardens.

alpine.ety: From Latin Alpīnus, from Alpēs (“the Alps”). Cognates include French alpin.

ex.en: Alpine flowers are abundant there.
ex.ja: そこは高山植物が豊富だ。

ex.en: He stood dazedly watching the beauty of the Alpine dawn.
ex.ja: 彼はアルプス山脈の夜明けの美しさをぼんやりとたたずんで見ていた。

ex.en: I like Alpine skiing better than Nordic skiing.
ex.ja: アルペンスキーの方がノルディックより好きです。

note.ja: ラテン語 Alpinus（アルプスの）から。「高山の」。

en: Encompassing on all sides; surrounding; encircling; enveloping.
Evoking or creating an atmosphere: atmospheric.
Something that surrounds; encompassing material, substance or shape.
The atmosphere; the surrounding air or sky; atmospheric components collectively such as air, clouds, water vapour, hail, etc.

ambient.ety: From Latin ambiēns (“going around”), from ambiō (“go around”).

ex.en: The ambient temperature in the room is twenty degrees.
ex.ja: 室内の温度は２０度だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 ambire（周りを回る）の現在分詞。amb（周り）+ ire（行く）。「周囲の」。ambition と同じ。

en: Relating to water; living in or near water, taking place in water.
Any aquatic plant.

Borrowed from Middle French aquatique (“living in water”), from Latin aquaticus (“relating to water”), from aqua (“water”).

ex.en: The lotus is an aquatic plant with very large leaves and flowers.
ex.ja: 蓮は、水生植物でとても大きな葉と花をつけます。

note.ja: ラテン語 aqua（水）+ -tic。「水生の」。aquarium、aqualung と同じ。

en: To declare with assurance or plainly and strongly; to state positively.
To use or exercise and thereby prove the existence of.
Synonym of assertion.

assert.ety: From Latin assertus, perfect passive participle of asserō (“declare someone free or a slave by laying hands upon him; hence free from, protect, defend; lay claim to, assert, declare”), from ad (“to”) + serō (“join, range in a row”).

ex.en: You'd better try to assert yourself more.
ex.ja: 君はもっと自己主張を試みたほうがよい。

ex.en: He asserts that she is innocent.
ex.ja: 彼は、彼女が無実だと主張している。

ex.en: He knows how to assert himself.
ex.ja: 彼は自己を没却する男ではない。

note.ja: ad（〜に）+ serere（結びつける）。「（自分のものだと）結びつける」→「主張する」。insert、series と同じ。

en: A person who does not believe in deities or gods.
A person who is certain that no deities exist or who thinks that the existence of deities can be disproven.
Of or relating to atheists or atheism; atheistic.

ex.ja: 彼は自分が無神論者だと告白した。

ex.en: No atheist worth his salt will try to prove that God does not exist.
ex.ja: まともな無神論者は、神の不存在を証明しようとはしない。

note.ja: a（否定）+ the（神）+ ist（人）。神を認めない人 →「無神論者」。

en: The width, usually measured in hertz, of a frequency band.
The width of the smallest frequency band within which the signal can fit.

ex.en: Video calls use a lot of bandwidth.
ex.ja: ビデオ通話は通信量を多く使う。

note.ja: band（帯）+ width（幅）。「周波数の帯の幅」→「帯域幅」→（人の）余力。

en: A fireplace or pit for grilling food, typically used outdoors and traditionally employing hot charcoal as the heating medium.
A meal or event highlighted by food cooked in such an apparatus.
To cook food on a barbecue; to smoke food over indirect heat from high-smoke fuels.
To grill.

barbecue.ety: From mid-17th century. Borrowed from Spanish barbacoa, from Taíno barbakoa (“framework of sticks”), the raised wooden structure the natives used to either sleep on or cure meat. Originally “meal of roasted meat or fish”. Doublet of balbacua and barbacoa.

ex.en: How about holding a barbecue party next Sunday?
ex.ja: 次の日曜にバーベキューパーティーをするのはどう？

ex.en: How about having a barbecue party next Sunday?
ex.ja: 次の日曜にバーベキューパーティーをするのはどう？

ex.en: We'll have a barbecue at the beach.
ex.ja: 海岸でバーベキューをしよう。

note.ja: スペイン語 barbacoa（木の焼き網）から。カリブの先住民の言葉に由来する。

en: At an earlier or preceding time.

beforehand.ety: From Middle English biforhand, biforhond, beforehonde, bifornhand, equivalent to before + hand. [13th century. After Old French avant main].

ex.en: How much of this did you know beforehand?
ex.ja: これについて、あなたは事前にどれくらい知っていましたか。

ex.en: Please let me know the schedule beforehand.
ex.ja: あらかじめ計画をお知らせください。

ex.en: Let's get things ready beforehand.
ex.ja: あらかじめ準備しておこうじゃないか。

note.ja: before（前に）+ hand。「手の前に」→「前もって」。

en: Involving or having both extremes or poles at the same time.
Relating to both polar regions.
A bipolar cell.

bipolar.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *dwóh₁
Proto-Indo-European *dwi-
Proto-Italic *dwi-
Latin bi-bor.
English bi-

From bi- + polar.

ex.en: He was diagnosed with bipolar disorder.
ex.ja: 彼は双極性障害と診断された。

note.ja: bi（2つの）+ polar（極の）。「双極の」→「双極性（障害）の」。

en: A flexible sac that can expand and contract and that holds liquids or gases.
Specifically, the urinary bladder.
To swell out like a bladder with air; to inflate.
To store or put up in bladders.

bladder.ety: From Middle English bladdre, bleddre, bladder, bledder, from Old English blæddre, a variant of blǣdre, blēdre (“blister, bladder”), from Proto-West Germanic *blādrā, from Proto-Germanic *blēdrǭ, *bladrǭ (“blister, bladder”).

ex.en: I have a weak bladder.
ex.ja: 僕、トイレが近いんだ。

ex.en: I had a bladder infection last month.
ex.ja: 先月膀胱炎にかかりました。

ex.en: For gall bladder surgery, go down this hall and take a right.
ex.ja: 胆のうの手術でしたら、この廊下をずっと行って右に曲がってください。

note.ja: 古英語 blǣdre（ふくらんだ袋）から。blow（吹く）と同系。「膀胱」。

en: A flower, especially one indicating that a fruit tree is fruiting; (collectively) a mass of such flowers.
The state or season of producing such flowers.
To have, or open into, blossoms; to bloom.
To begin to thrive or flourish.

blossom.ety: From Middle English blosme, from Old English blostm, blostma, from Proto-Germanic *blōstmô (compare West Frisian blossem, Dutch bloesem; related to *blōstaz [compare German Blust]), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰleh₃-s- (“bloom, flower”), from *bʰleh₃- (“to bloom, to thrive”). Cognate with Albanian bleron (“to blossom, to thrive”), Latin flōs (“flower”), Flōra (“goddess of plants”). See more at blow (etymology 4).

ex.en: The blossoms expand under the influence of the weather.
ex.ja: 花は天気の影響を受けて開く。

ex.en: The apple tree has a beautiful blossom.
ex.ja: リンゴの木が美しい花を咲かせている。

ex.en: The blossoms will be out in a few days.
ex.ja: ２、３日すれば開花するでしょう。

note.ja: 古英語 blōstm（花）から。bloom、blow（花が咲く）と同系。

en: A convoy or procession of travellers, their cargo and vehicles, and any pack animals, especially camels crossing a desert.
A furnished vehicle towed behind a car, etc., and used as a dwelling when stationary.
To travel in a caravan (procession).
To travel and/or live in a caravan (vehicle).

caravan.ety:
From Middle French caravane, from Old French carvane, from Persian کاروان (kârvân), from Middle Persian kʾlwʾn' (kārawān), from Old Persian 𐎣𐎠𐎼 (k-a-r, “people, subjects”).
The word was used to designate a group of people who were travelling by camel or horse on the Silk Road. Doublet of Kairouan.

ex.en: Dogs bark when the caravan passes by.
ex.ja: 犬は吠えても隊商は進む。

ex.en: A caravan of fifty camels slowly made its way through the desert.
ex.ja: ５０頭の駱駝から成る隊商が砂漠の中をゆっくりと進んでいた。

note.ja: ペルシャ語 kārwān（隊商）から。「隊商」→ 移動する住まい →「キャンピングカー」。van はこの短縮。

en: Singing, especially as a chant is sung.

chanting.ety: From Middle English chauntynge; equivalent to chant + -ing.

ex.en: The chanting of the crowd grew louder.
ex.ja: 群衆のシュプレヒコールがだんだん大きくなった。

note.ja: chant（唱える）+ -ing。ラテン語 cantare（歌う）。「詠唱」。enchant と同じ。

en: Pressed tightly together.
Flattened, especially when along its entire length.

ex.en: Send it to me as a compressed file.
ex.ja: 圧縮したファイルを添付で送ってください。

ex.en: The gas was compressed into a gas cylinder.
ex.ja: その気体は圧縮されてボンベに詰め込まれた。

note.ja: compress（圧縮する）+ -ed。com + premere（押す）。press と同じ。

en: Of or relating to computation.

computational.ety:

note.ja: law（法）+ -ful。「合法の」。

en: One who makes or enacts laws.

lawmaker.ety: From Middle English lawemaker, lawe maker, equivalent to law + maker.

ex.en: Lawmakers debated the new bill for hours.
ex.ja: 議員たちはその新しい法案を何時間も議論した。

note.ja: law（法律）+ maker（作る人）。「立法者・議員」。

en: In a loose manner.
Not tightly.

loosely.ety: From Middle English lously; equivalent to loose + -ly.

ex.en: The movie is loosely based on a true story.
ex.ja: その映画は実話を大まかに基にしている。

note.ja: loose（ゆるい）+ -ly。「ゆるく・大まかに」。

en: Any member of the genus Nelumbo of aquatic plants in the family Nelumbonaceae.
A water lily (Nymphaea), especially those of Egypt or India.

lotus.ety: Unadapted borrowing from Latin lōtus, from Ancient Greek λωτός (lōtós). Doublet of lote. First attested in the 1540s. Ultimately from Hebrew לוֹט (lōṭ, “myrrh”, literally “covering, envelope”).

ex.en: Can you sit in the Lotus position?
ex.ja: あなた、結跏趺坐ができますか？

ex.en: We have very big lotus leaves.
ex.ja: こちらには大きなハスの葉があります。

ex.en: The lotus is an aquatic plant with very large leaves and flowers.
ex.ja: 蓮は、水生植物でとても大きな葉と花をつけます。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 lōtos から。「ハス」。

en: A piece of clothing somewhat like an open robe or cloak, especially that worn by Orthodox bishops.
A figurative garment representing authority or status, capable of affording protection.
To cover or conceal (something); to cloak; to disguise.
To become covered or concealed.

mantle.ety: From Middle English mantel, from Old English mæntel, mentel (“sleeveless cloak”), from Proto-West Germanic *mantel; later reinforced by Anglo-Norman mantel, both from Latin mantellum (“covering, cloak”) (French manteau), diminutive of mantum (Spanish manto), probably from Gaulish *mantos, *mantalos (“trodden road”), from Proto-Celtic *mantos, *mantlos, from Proto-Indo-European *menH- (“tread, press together; crumble”). Compare Icelandic möttull. Doublet of manteau.

ex.en: She took on the mantle of team captain.
ex.ja: 彼女はチームの主将という重責を引き受けた。

note.ja: ラテン語 mantellum（外套）から。mantel（マントルピース）も同じ。地球の「マントル」は外側を覆う層から。

en: Something thought to bring good luck.
Something, especially a person or animal, used to symbolize a sports team, company, organization or other group.
To act as a mascot (for).

mascot.ety: Borrowed from French mascotte, from Occitan mascòta (“sortilege”), feminine diminutive of masca (“witch”), from Old Occitan masca, from Medieval Latin masca (“specter, nightmare”). More at mask.

ex.en: This dog is our regimental mascot.
ex.ja: この犬は我が連隊のマスコットだ。

note.ja: プロヴァンス語 mascoto（魔よけ）から。「幸運を呼ぶもの」→「マスコット」。

en: Of or pertaining to metabolism.
A nutritional supplement.

metabolic.ety: Borrowed from Ancient Greek μεταβολικός (metabolikós), from μεταβολή (metabolḗ, “change”) + -ικός (-ikós), thus by surface analysis, metabola + -ic. Compare metabolism.

ex.en: Exercise increases your metabolic rate.
ex.ja: 運動すると代謝率が上がる。

note.ja: metabolism（代謝）+ -ic。ギリシャ語 metabolē（変化）。「代謝の」。

en: The portion of a team which typically plays centrally, between the attack (or forwards) and the defence (or backs).
The middle of the field of play.

midfield.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *-dʰe
Proto-Indo-European *médʰi

Proto-West Germanic *felþu

English midfield
From mid- + field.

ex.en: The battle for the ball took place in midfield.
ex.ja: ボールの奪い合いはフィールドの中盤で繰り広げられた。

note.ja: mid（中央）+ field（フィールド）。「競技場の中央部」。

en: Fighting or disposed to fight; belligerent, warlike.
Aggressively supporting of an idea, group, political or social cause, etc.; adamant, combative.
An entrenched or aggressive adherent to a particular cause, now especially a member of a particular ideological faction.
Someone who supports the Trotskyist political view expressed in the newspaper Militant.

militant.ety: From Middle French militant, from Latin mīlitāns, present participle of mīlitāre (“to serve as a soldier”).

ex.en: A militant group attacked the town.
ex.ja: 過激派のグループがその町を襲撃した。

note.ja: ラテン語 militare（兵役に就く）から。miles（兵士）。「戦闘的な・過激派」。military と同じ。

en: A longing for home or familiar surroundings; homesickness.
A bittersweet yearning for the things of the past.

nostalgia.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *nes-
Proto-Indo-European *-tós
Proto-Hellenic *nóstos
Ancient Greek νόστος (nóstos)
Proto-Indo-European *h₂leg-der.?
Ancient Greek ἄλγος (álgos)
▲
German Heimwehcalq.
New Latin nostalgiabor.
English nostalgia
From New Latin nostalgia, coined by Johannes Hofer in 1688 from Ancient Greek νόστος (nóstos, “returning home”) + ἄλγος (álgos, “pain”), calquing German Heimweh. Ancient Greek *νοσταλγία (*nostalgía) is unattested. Transferred sense probably influenced by French nostalgie, especially in literature.
Compare Italian nostalgia, Spanish nostalgia, Portugues

ex.en: Returning to your hometown after a long time fills you with nostalgia.
ex.ja: 久しぶりに故郷に帰ると、懐かしい気持ちが込み上がる。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 nostos（帰郷）+ algos（痛み）。「故郷に帰りたい痛み」→「郷愁・懐かしさ」。neuralgia（神経痛）の -algia も同じ。

en: An upholstered sofa, without arms or a back, sometimes with a compartment for storing linen etc.
A low stool or thick cushion used to rest the feet or as a seat.

ottoman.ety: From Ottoman in the early 19th century; so named because reclining on a couch was associated with Middle Eastern customs.

ex.en: Constantinople fell to the hands of the Ottoman Turks in 1453.
ex.ja: 1453年、コンスタンティノープルはオスマン帝国の手に渡った。

note.ja: オスマン帝国（Ottoman Empire）から。トルコ風の低いソファー →「足置き」。Ottoman は創始者オスマン1世の名。

en: Rough or unhusked rice, either before it is milled or as a crop to be harvested.
A paddy field, a rice paddy; an irrigated or flooded field where rice is grown.

paddy.ety: Borrowed from Malay padi (“paddy plant”). Doublet of palay.

ex.en: Hey, you wanna go check out the terraced rice paddies?
ex.ja: ねぇ、棚田を見に行ってみない？

ex.en: Hey, do you want to go see the terraced rice paddies?
ex.ja: ねぇ、棚田を見に行ってみない？

note.ja: マレー語 padi（稲）から。「水田」。

en: A book with flexible binding.
Having flexible binding.
To issue or publish (a book) in a paperback edition.

paperback.ety: From paper + back, a shortening of the older term paper-backed book.

ex.en: Is there a paperback edition of this book?
ex.ja: この本のペーパーバック版はありますか。

ex.en: It's best to put covers on paperbacks.
ex.ja: 文庫本にカバーをかけた方がいいです。

note.ja: paper（紙）+ back（背表紙）。「紙表紙の本」。hardcover の対。

en: Covered in pavement; having a hard surface, as of concrete or asphalt.
Laid out or made, as intentions, desires, plans, etc.

paved.ety: From Middle English paved, ypavyd, equivalent to pave + -ed.

ex.en: Next year, this gravel road will be paved.
ex.ja: この砂利道は来年舗装されるだろう。

ex.en: The road to hell is paved with good intentions.
ex.ja: 地獄への道は善意で敷かれている。

ex.en: The road to Hell is paved with good intentions.
ex.ja: 地獄への道は善意で敷かれている。

note.ja: pave（舗装する）+ -ed。ラテン語 pavire（たたき固める）。pavement と同じ。

en: An ornate tent.
A light roofed structure used as a shelter in a public place.
To furnish with a pavilion.
To put inside a pavilion.

pavilion.ety:
From Middle English pavilloun, from Anglo-Norman pavilloun, from Latin pāpiliōnem, form of pāpiliō (“butterfly, moth”) (due to resemblance of tent to a butterfly’s wings), of unknown origin. Doublet of papilio and papillon.
Cognate to French pavillon (“pavilion”) and papillon (“butterfly”), and similar terms in other Romance languages.

ex.en: When I was young, my father often talked to me about the Golden Pavilion.
ex.ja: 幼時から父は、私によく、金閣のことを語った。

ex.en: The beauty of the Golden Pavilion covered in snow was unmatched.
ex.ja: 雪に包まれた金閣の美しさは、比べるものがなかった。

note.ja: ラテン語 papilio（蝶）から。蝶が羽を広げたような「テント」→「パビリオン・展示館」。

en: Perquisite.
A bonus ability that a player character can acquire; a permanent power-up.
To make (coffee) in a percolator or a drip coffeemaker.
Of coffee: to be produced by heated water seeping (“percolating”) through coffee grounds.

ex.en: There's the perk of letting you join communities for paying members.
ex.ja: 有料会員専用のコミュに入会出来る特典があります。

note.ja: perquisite（臨時収入）の短縮。「特典・役得」。perk up（元気になる）は別語。

en: One who points.
A teacher's pointer, pointing stick, a rod with an arrow.

pointer.ety: From point + -er (agent noun suffix) or + -er (measurement suffix) (sense 4).

ex.en: Our pointer took off after a big deer.
ex.ja: 私たちの猟犬は大きな鹿を追いかけた。

ex.en: Every time I attempt to teach myself C++, I get stuck on pointers.
ex.ja: Ｃ＋＋を学ぼうとするたびに、ポインタに手こずる。

ex.en: The compass pointer always seeks north.
ex.ja: 羅針盤の針は常に北を示す。

note.ja: point（指す）+ -er。「指示棒」→ 画面の「ポインター」→「助言」。

en: To be so presumptuous as (to do something) without proper authority or permission [with to (+ infinitive)].
To assume or suggest to be true (without proof); to take for granted, to suppose.

presume.ety: From Middle English presumen, from Anglo-Norman presumer and its source, Latin praesūmere (“to take beforehand, anticipate”), from prae- + sūmere (“to take”).

ex.en: I will not presume to give an opinion.
ex.ja: あえて意見を述べることはよしておこう。

ex.en: Tom is still married to Mary, I presume.
ex.ja: トムはまだメアリーと結婚してるよ。私が推測するに。

ex.en: I presume that he has paid the money back.
ex.ja: 彼はお金を返したと思う。

note.ja: pre（前もって）+ sum（取る）+ e。前もって取る →「推定する・思い込む」。

en: One who has committed rape; someone who raped another person.

rapist.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *-idyéti

From rape + -ist.

ex.ja: 警察はついに強姦犯を逮捕した。

note.ja: rape（強姦する）+ -ist。rape はラテン語 rapere（奪い去る）。rapid、rapture と同じ。

en: Having a shape like a rectangle.
Having axes that meet each other with right angles.

rectangular.ety:

ex.ja: そのテーブルは丸ではなく長方形だ。

note.ja: rectangle（長方形）+ -ar。ラテン語 rectus（まっすぐな・直角の）+ angulus（角）。「直角の角を持つ」。rect、angle と同じ。

en: A device that controls or limits something.
A person or group that sets standards of practice, especially regulatory law as sanctioned by statutory law.

From regulate + -or.

ex.en: There was a flare-up between local residents and state regulators.
ex.ja: 地元住民と政府調査官の間に折衝がありました。

note.ja: regulate + -or。「規制機関・調整器」。

en: A reorganization; an alteration of structure.

ex.en: Research in Motion announced the layoff of 2000 employees and a restructuring of the company.
ex.ja: リサーチ・イン・モーションが約２千人の従業員解雇と組織再編を発表した。

ex.en: Thank to a fundamental restructuring, our surplus has swelled threefold.
ex.ja: 抜本的に事業の再構築を行ったおかげで、当社の黒字は３倍に膨らんだ。

ex.en: Thanks to a fundamental restructuring, our surplus has swelled three-fold.
ex.ja: 抜本的な合理化のおかげで、わが社の利益は３倍に増えた。

note.ja: re（再び）+ structure（構造）+ -ing。「構造を組み直すこと」→「再編・リストラ」。

en: A deliberate action aimed at weakening someone (or something, a nation, etc) or preventing them from being successful, through subversion…
To deliberately destroy or damage something in order to prevent it from being successful.

ex.en: Someone tried to sabotage the machine.
ex.ja: 誰かがその機械を壊そうとした。

note.ja: フランス語 saboter（木靴でぶち壊す）から。sabot（木靴）。「破壊工作・妨害」。

en: Use of acerbic language to mock or convey contempt, often using verbal irony and (in speech) often marked by overemphasis and sneering.
An individual act of the above.

From Late Latin sarcasmus, from Ancient Greek σαρκασμός (sarkasmós, “a sneer”), from σαρκάζω (sarkázō, “to gnash the teeth (in anger)”, literally “to strip off the flesh”), from σάρξ (sárx, “flesh”).

ex.en: That might sound like sarcasm.
ex.ja: それは皮肉に聞こえちゃうかもね。

ex.en: She doesn't understand sarcasm.
ex.ja: 彼女は皮肉を解さない。

ex.en: He spoke with a suggestion of sarcasm in his voice.
ex.ja: 彼は少しばかり皮肉っぽく話した。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 sarkazein（肉を引き裂く）から。sarx（肉）。「肉を裂くような言葉」→「皮肉」。sarcastic。

en: One who seeks.
Especially, a religious seeker: a pilgrim, or one who aspires to enlightenment or salvation.

seeker.ety:
From Middle English sekar, sekere (also sechar, sechere), from Old English *sēċare, from Proto-West Germanic *sōkārī, from Proto-Germanic *sōkārijaz. Equivalent to seek + -er.
Cognate with Dutch zoeker, German Sucher, German Low German Söker, Gothic 𐍃𐍉𐌺𐌰𐍂𐌴𐌹𐍃 (sōkareis), Norwegian søker, Saterland Frisian Säiker, West Frisian syker, and Yiddish זוכער (zukher).

ex.en: The island is popular with thrill seekers.
ex.ja: その島はスリルを求める人々に人気がある。

note.ja: seek（探す）+ -er。「探し求める人」。

en: Unfairly discriminatory against one sex in favour of the other.
A person who discriminates on grounds of sex; someone who practises sexism.

ex.en: The company apologized for its sexist advertisement.
ex.ja: その会社は性差別的な広告について謝罪した。

note.ja: sex（性）+ -ist。racist（人種差別主義者）にならった語。「性差別的な」。

en: The action of stopping operations; a closing, of a computer, business, event, etc.
A statement, insult, etc. that prevents the opponent from replying further.

ex.en: The government shutdown closed many offices.
ex.ja: 政府機関の閉鎖で多くの事務所が閉まった。

note.ja: shut down（閉じる・停止する）の名詞化。「停止・閉鎖」。

en: To go beyond or exceed (something) in an adjudicative or literal sense.

surpass.ety: From Middle French surpasser (“to pass beyond”). By surface analysis, sur- + pass. Displaced native Old English oferstīgan (literally “to climb over”).

ex.en: Japan surpasses China in economic power.
ex.ja: 日本の経済力で、中国より勝っている。

ex.en: She surpasses her sister in beauty.
ex.ja: 彼女は美しさという点では姉はしのいでいる。

ex.en: The view from the mountain top far surpassed our expectations.
ex.ja: 山頂からの眺めは、期待をはるかに上回るものだった。

note.ja: sur（超えて）+ pass（通る）。「越えて通り過ぎる」→「上回る」。

en: Target sighted.
One of two books, sheets of paper, etc., on which corresponding accounts were kept.
Any account or score kept by notches or marks, whether on wood or paper, or in a book, especially one kept in duplicate.
To count something.
To mathematically calculate a numeric result.

ex.en: Keep a tally of what you owe.
ex.ja: いくら借りているか記録をつけておきなさい。

note.ja: ラテン語 talea（棒切れ）から。刻み目をつけた棒で数を記録したことから「集計・記録」。

ex.en: Tom tucked his shirt into his pants.
ex.ja: トムはシャツをズボンの中に入れた。

ex.en: He tucked the handkerchief in his pocket.
ex.ja: 彼はそのハンカチをポケットに押し込んだ。

ex.en: He tucked the napkin under his chin.
ex.ja: 彼はあごの下にナプキンをはさみ込んだ。

note.ja: tuck（押し込む）+ -ed。古英語 tūcian（虐待する）から意味が変わった。「しまい込まれた」。

unanimously.ety:

From unanimous + -ly.

ex.ja: 彼のばかげた提案が満場一致で承認された。

en: Never defeated; always victorious.

undefeated.ety:

From un- + defeated.

ex.ja: そのチームは今シーズンまだ負けていない。

note.ja: un（否定）+ defeated（負けた）。「無敗の」。

en: Strange, not familiar.
An unfamiliar person; a stranger.

unfamiliar.ety:
Etymology tree

Proto-Germanic *un-

From un- + familiar.

ex.en: The cat was scared by an unfamiliar noise.
ex.ja: その猫は聞き慣れない物音がしたのでびっくりした。

ex.en: The voice on the phone was unfamiliar to me.
ex.ja: 電話の声は私には聞き覚えのないものだった。

ex.en: The landscape is unfamiliar to me.
ex.ja: それは私が見たことのない景色だ。

note.ja: un（否定）+ familiar（なじみのある）。familiar はラテン語 familia（家族）。「家族のようになじんでいない」。

en: Greatly, in a vast manner.

vastly.ety:
Etymology tree
English vast
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English vastly
From vast + -ly.

ex.en: These two are vastly different from each other.
ex.ja: これら二つの間には大きな違いがある。

ex.en: I think this suit is vastly superior to that one in quality.
ex.ja: この服は品質においてあの服よりも優れていると思う。

note.ja: vast（広大な）+ -ly。「大いに」。

en: Morally low; base; despicable.
Causing physical or mental repulsion; horrid; disgusting.
That which is vile; vileness.

vile.ety: From Middle English vile, vyle, vyl, from Anglo-Norman ville, Old French vil, vile, from Latin vīlis.

ex.en: The food smelled vile.
ex.ja: その食べ物はひどいにおいがした。

note.ja: ラテン語 vilis（安い・価値のない）から。「ひどく不快な・卑劣な」。

en: In a violent manner.
To an intense degree; extremely; strongly; intensely.

violently.ety: From Middle English violently; equivalent to violent + -ly.

ex.en: I felt my heart beating violently.
ex.ja: 僕は心臓が激しく打っているのを感じた。

ex.en: I felt my heart beat violently.
ex.ja: 私は心臓が激しく打つのを感じた。

ex.en: The views of the two politicians collide violently.
ex.ja: 二人の政治家の見解は激しく激突している。

note.ja: violent + -ly。「激しく・乱暴に」。

en: One of the simple machines; a piece of material, such as metal or wood, thick at one edge and tapered to a thin edge at the other for ins…
A piece (of food, metal, wood etc.) having this shape.
To support or secure using a wedge.
To force into a narrow gap.

wedge.ety: From Middle English wegge (“wedge”), from Old English weċġ (“wedge”), from Proto-West Germanic *wagi, from Proto-Germanic *wagjaz.

ex.en: Would you like another wedge of pie?
ex.ja: パイをもう一ついかがですか。

ex.en: The screw, the lever, the wedge, the pulley, etc. are called simple machines.
ex.ja: ねじ、てこ、くさび、滑車などは単一機械と呼ばれる。

note.ja: 古英語 wecg（くさび）から。「くさび・くさび形のもの」。

en: In a wise manner; using good judgement.

wisely.ety: From Middle English wisliche, wislike, from Old English wīslīċe (“wisely”, adverb), equivalent to wise + -ly.

ex.en: So use it wisely and don't waste it.
ex.ja: 無駄使いしないようにね。計画的に使ってね。

ex.en: I want to spend my free time wisely.
ex.ja: 余暇の時間は有意義に過ごしたいです。

ex.en: If wisely used, money can do much.
ex.ja: もし上手に使えば、お金はずいぶん役に立つ。

note.ja: wise + -ly。「賢明に」。

Capable of being adapted or of adapting; susceptible of or undergoing accordant change.

ex.ja: その動物には色が変わる環境に適した毛皮がある。

zh: 使人成癮的 /使人成瘾的

en: Causing or tending to cause addiction; habit-forming.
Enjoyable, so that one comes back for more.
A drug that causes an addiction.
Anything that is very habit-forming.

addictive.ety: First attested 1914. Addiction in modern sense is first attested 1906, in reference to opium. There is an isolated instance from 1779, with reference to tobacco.

ex.en: Is nicotine as addictive as heroin?
ex.ja: ニコチンはヘロインと同様に中毒性があるのですか？

note.ja: addict（中毒にする）+ -ive。ラテン語 addicere（引き渡す）、ad + dicere（言う）。「（主人に）引き渡された」→「とりこになった」。

en: A natural attraction or feeling of kinship to a person or thing.
A family relationship through marriage of a relative (e.g. sister-in-law), as opposed to consanguinity (e.g. sister).

affinity.ety: From Middle English affinite, from Old French affinité. Ostensibly equivalent to affine + -ity. See also af-.

ex.en: This case has an affinity with that one.
ex.ja: この事件はあの事件と似たところがある。

ex.en: They feel a strange affinity with each other.
ex.ja: 彼らは妙におたがいに気が合う。

ex.en: I feel a strong affinity for her.
ex.ja: 彼女がとても好きです。

note.ja: ラテン語 affinis（境を接する・姻戚の）から。ad + finis（境界）。「隣り合った」→「親近感・相性」。final と同じ fin。

en: A metal that is a combination of two or more elements, at least one of which is a metal, a base metal.
An admixture; something added which stains, taints etc.
To mix or combine; often used of metals.
To reduce the purity of by mixing with a less valuable substance.

alloy.ety: Borrowed from Middle French alloy, aloy, from Old French aloi, from aloiier, from Latin alligō.

ex.en: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.
ex.ja: 真鍮は銅と亜鉛の合金である。

ex.en: Bronze-ware is largely made from alloys of brass and tin.
ex.ja: 青銅器は主として銅と錫の合金で出来ている。

ex.en: ODS super alloy is produced by the mechanical alloy method following powder metallurgy.
ex.ja: ＯＤＳスーパーアロイは粉末冶金技術を伴うメカニカルアロイ法により製造されます。

note.ja: 古フランス語 aloi（混ぜること）から。ラテン語 alligare（結びつける）。「合金」。ally（同盟する）と同じ。

ja: アパルトヘイト（人種隔離政策）

en: The policy of racial segregation in South Africa from 1948 to 1994.
Any similar policy of racial segregation or separation and discrimination, particularly when in favor of a minority rule.
To impose a policy of segregation of groups of people, especially one based on race.

ex.en: Nelson Mandela fought against apartheid.
ex.ja: ネルソン・マンデラはアパルトヘイトと闘った。

note.ja: アフリカーンス語で「分離（apart + heid）」。南アフリカの人種隔離政策。

en: Inflammation of a joint or joints causing pain and/or disability, swelling and stiffness, and due to various causes such as infection, tr…

arthritis.ety: From Latin arthrītis, from Ancient Greek ἀρθρῖτις (arthrîtis, “joint-disease, gout”), from ἄρθρον (árthron, “a joint”). By surface analysis, arthr- + -itis.

ex.en: My grandmother has arthritis in her knees.
ex.ja: 祖母はひざに関節炎がある。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 arthron（関節）+ -itis（炎症）。「関節炎」。arthropod（節足動物）と同じ arthr。

ex.en: Only the manager can authorise a refund.
ex.ja: 払い戻しを認める権限があるのは支配人だけだ。

note.ja: authorize のイギリスのつづり。author（作り出す人）と同じ。「権限を与える」。

en: Evil, especially considered as an active force for destruction or death.
Suffering, woe, torment.
To wrap into a bale.

bale.ety:
From Middle English bale (“evil”), from Old English bealu, from Proto-West Germanic *balu, from Proto-Germanic *balwą.
Cognate with Low German bal- (“bad, ill”), Gothic 𐌱𐌰𐌻𐍅𐌴𐌹𐌽𐍃 (balweins, “torture”), Old High German balo (“destruction”), Old Norse bǫl (“disaster”).

ex.en: The farmer stacked bales of hay in the barn.
ex.ja: 農夫は干し草の束を納屋に積み上げた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 bale（包み）から。ball と同系。「（干し草などの）俵」。

en: A semiaquatic rodent of the genus Castor, having a wide, flat tail and webbed feet, native to the Northern Hemisphere.
The fur of the beaver.
To form a felt-like texture, similar to the way beaver fur is used for felt-making.
To work hard.

beaver.ety:
From Middle English bever, from Old English befer, from Proto-West Germanic *bebru, from Proto-Germanic *bebruz, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰébʰrus (“beaver”).
Cognate with West Frisian bever, Dutch bever, French bièvre, German Biber, dialectal Swedish bjur. Non-Germanic cognates include Welsh befer, Latin fiber, Lithuanian bẽbras, Russian бобр (bobr), Avestan 𐬠𐬀𐬎𐬎𐬭𐬀 (bauura), and Sanskrit बभ्रु (bábhru, “mongoose; ichneumon”).
Slang use to refer to a woman evolved from use to refer to pubic hair, which evolved from use to refer to beards, which evolved from use to refer to the furry animal or

ex.en: Beavers rarely inflict damage on people.
ex.ja: ビーバーは人に危害を加えることはめったにない。

ex.en: He is an eager beaver.
ex.ja: 彼は仕事の鬼だ。

ex.en: Rabbits are related to beavers and squirrels.
ex.ja: ウサギはビーバーやリスと同族です。

note.ja: 古英語 beofor から。brown と同じ祖先で「茶色の動物」の意。

en: A brag; ostentatious positive appraisal of oneself.
Something that one brags about.
To brag; to talk loudly in praise of oneself.
[with about or of] To speak of with pride, vanity, or exultation, with a view to self-commendation; to extol.

boast.ety:
From Middle English bosten, from bost (“boast, glory, noise, arrogance, presumption, pride, vanity”), probably of North Germanic origin, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *bausuz (“inflated, swollen, puffed up, proud, arrogant, bad”).
Cognate with Scots bost, boist (“to threaten, brag, boast”), Anglo-Norman bost (“ostentation”) (from Germanic). Related to Norwegian baus (“proud, bold, daring”), dialectal German baustern (“to swell”), German böse (“evil, bad, angry”), Dutch boos (“evil, wicked, angry”), West Frisian boas (“bad, wicked, angry, shrewd, clever”). Compare also dialectal Norwegian baus

ex.en: I am sick to death of his boasts.
ex.ja: 彼の自慢話はまったく聞き飽きた。

ex.en: He boasted of having won the first prize.
ex.ja: 彼は１等をとった事を自慢した。

ex.en: He boasts that he can speak six languages.
ex.ja: 彼は６ヶ国語を話すことができると自慢している。

note.ja: 中英語 bost から。語源ははっきりしない。「自慢する」。

en: The person who makes a telephone call.
A visitor.

caller.ety: From Middle English callar, equivalent to call + -er.

ex.en: The caller refused to give us his name.
ex.ja: 電話をかけた者は名前を教えるのを拒否した。

ex.en: The caller hung up without saying anything.
ex.ja: 相手は何も言わずに電話を切ったんだ。

ex.en: He was besieged by callers.
ex.ja: 彼は来客攻めにあった。

note.ja: call（呼ぶ・電話する）+ -er。「電話をかける人・訪問者」。

en: A hollow area within the body.
The female part of a mold: the depression itself or (metonymically) the half of the mold that contains it.

cavity.ety: From Middle French cavité or Late Latin cavitās, from cav(i) (“hollow, excavated, concave”) + -tās (“-ity”, nominal suffix). First attested in the Mid-16th c.

ex.en: I have a lot of cavities now.
ex.ja: 今は虫歯だらけだ。

ex.en: If we care for our teeth we won't have cavities.
ex.ja: 歯をきちんと手入れしていれば虫歯にはならない。

ex.en: I think I have a cavity.
ex.ja: どうも虫歯のようです。

note.ja: ラテン語 cavus（空洞の）から。「空洞・虫歯」。cave（洞穴）と同じ。

en: A man, a fellow.
A child.
Of the skin, to split or flake due to cold weather or dryness.
To cause to open in slits or chinks; to split; to cause the skin of to crack or become rough.

chap.ety: Clipping of chapman (“dealer, customer”) in 16th-century English.

ex.en: In the winter, my lips would chap.
ex.ja: 冬になると唇が割れたりする。

ex.en: Lips chap in winter.
ex.ja: 冬になると唇が割れたりする。

note.ja: chapman（行商人）の短縮。「客・相手」→（英）「やつ・男」。cheap と同系。

en: A young male horse or similar young male equine, especially just after birth or less than a year old.
A young crane (bird).
To frisk or frolic like a colt; to act licentiously or wantonly.

colt.ety: From Middle English colt, from Old English colt, from Proto-Germanic *kultaz (“plump; stump; thick shape, bulb”), from Proto-Indo-European *gelt- (“something round, pregnant belly, child in the womb”), from *gel- (“to ball up, amass”). Cognate with Faroese koltur (“colt, foal”) Norwegian kult (“treestump”), Swedish kult (“young boar, piglet, boy, lad”) / Swedish kulting (“piglet”). Related to child.

ex.en: The wildest colt makes the best horse.
ex.ja: 最も野性的な子馬が最高の駿馬になる。

note.ja: 古英語 colt（子馬）から。「雄の子馬」。銃のコルトは人名から。

en: A public building housing courts of law.
The public building where most American counties have their county offices.

ex.en: Were you at the courthouse?
ex.ja: 裁判所にいたの？

ex.en: "You can get it at the courthouse," the clerk added.
ex.ja: 「都庁舎でもらえますよ」と係員が付け加えた。

ex.en: The woman left and went to the courthouse, where she waited in line again.
ex.ja: 都庁舎に行き、そこでまた列の中で待った。

note.ja: court（裁判所）+ house（建物）。「裁判所の建物」。

en: Strange; weird; odd.
Sick; unwell.
An ill-tempered or nasty person.
A twist or turn of the mind; caprice; whim.
To turn by means of a crank.
To turn a crank.

crank.ety: From Dutch or Low German krank, ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *krank, from Proto-Germanic *krangaz, *krankaz (“bent; weak”). Cognate with Scots crank, krank, German krank (“sick”).

ex.en: An office machine is cranking out a stream of documents.
ex.ja: 事務機が書類を次々とプリントアウトしている。

ex.en: Hey! I don't want any crank calls - not at this hour.
ex.ja: こんな夜遅くにいたずら電話をかけてくるなよな。

ex.en: What a crank he is!
ex.ja: なんてつむじ曲がりなやつだ。

note.ja: 古英語 cranc（曲がった）とされる。「クランク」→ 考えが曲がった「変人」→（crank up）回して強める。
